topics.title: Number Theory?
topics.text:
We will call a number $N$ green if $6*N$ contains none of the digits $0$, $1$, $2$, $3$, and $4$. There are two digits such that every green number contains at least one of them. One of these two digits is $1$. What is the other?



This is from the getset amc, for the australian mathematics competition

Please help.

Here is the solution that they provided. I don't get it starting from assuming the leftmost is 8The rightmost digit must be $1$ or $3$ or $6$ or $8$. If the leftmost digit of $N$ is $a$ and 2≤a≤7, the leftmost digit of $6N$ will be one of the digits: $1$, $2$, $3$, $4$



Now assume that the leftmost digit of $N$ is $8$. Then 8×10k≤N<9×10k for some non-negative integer k.



Hence 48×10k≤6N<54×10k, and therefore either the leftmost digit of $6N$ or its second leftmost digit is one of the digits:$0$, $1$, $2$, $3$, $4$. So the leftmost digit of $N$ is either $1$ or $9$.



Hence the digit in question must be $9$.

topics.title: Sliding Triangles
topics.text:
IMAGE

The triangle above lies on a flat surface and is pushed at the top vertex. The length of the congruent sides does not change, but the angle between the two congruent sides will increase, and the base will stretch. Initially, the area of the triangle will increase, but eventually, the area will decrease, continuing until the triangle collapses.



What is the maximum area achieved during this process? And, what is the length of the base when this process is used to create a different triangle whose area is the same as the triangle above?

SolutionSolution: 200 square units; 32 units.



For the first part of the question, the maximum area occurs when the angle between the sides is a right angle. (This is often true for geometry questions involving maximum area:  of all quadrilaterals with a given perimeter, the one with maximum area is a square.)

The area of a triangle can be calculated by taking half the product of two sides and the sine of the angle between those sides, so the area of any triangle will be greatest when the sine of the included angle is greatest. The sine reaches its maximum, 1, when the angle is 90°, so a right triangle will produce the greatest area.



For the second part of the question, note that if you bisect the original triangle, divide it into two right triangles, and rearrange the pieces, you can form a new triangle with exactly the same area. The original triangle had a height of 16 (found through the Pythagorean theorem) and a base of 24, so its area is ½(16)(24) = 192 square units. Likewise, the new triangle has a height of 12 and a base of 32, so its area is also ½(12)(32) = 192 square units.

topics.title: Help...in Life
topics.text:
Ever since I was in elementary school, I knew I was different from all the kids.  I was at least two grades ahead, and I was usually teased for it.  However the intelligence, I was totally ignorant to the smart kids all around the U.S.,who, even in 4th grade, were doing advanced math like Algebra 1 and 2 and were preparing for contests like the AMC 8 and Mathcounts.  I admit it, I was very blind to what I should have been doing.  I thought that I could be successful even if I was just "above average".  I had no idea that I also needed to compare myself with those smarter than me.  Now, I am completely behind  the kids out there who do these competitions.



I regret to say that I am entering 8th grade, and I have only taken the AMC 8 once, last year.  I also regret to say that I got only a 17 on the AMC 8, and as for MathCounts, well, forget it.  My school, being one of the pioneers of the Common Core, thought it wasn't a good idea.  However, thanks to my mom, I was able to take the AMC 8.  She helped convince the school board so that we could be given a chance.  And I blew that chance.  I am now going into 8th grade, dazed, at how behind I am.  I hear kids all the time (obviously on AoPS, my school mates don't even know what the AMC is) say they easily ace the AMC and Mathcounts, and have no problem with getting to State or Nationals.  I wish I could say that myself.  Yet I sit here today, at my Dell computer, trying to catch up.  My school, judging by our performance last year, will probably not enter any contests.



I may be the smartest kid in the school, but this is a small feat.  Compared to the kids on this forum and those taking more contests, I might as well be in Special Education.  In my opinion, if I can't enter and do good in math contests, I won't be able to be recognized by colleges.



What I ask for you is not to take pity, but to give me your advice and your knowledge about Math Contests and good math techniques.  Judging by my situation, how can I be sure to take the AMC 8, AMC 10, Mathcounts, etc., and, more importantly, do very well on them?  I desperately need this knowledge, because I am already behind, and I can never achieve my dream of reaching the IMO or getting into this prestigious Math/Engineering Academy without it.



Thank you in advance, and hopefully you can learn from this and start earlier.

[code]Q1: At a dance party a group of boys and girls exchange dances as follows: one boy dances with 5 girls, a second boy dances with 6 girls, and so on, the last boy dancing with all the girls. If b represents the number of boys and g the number of girls, then find b in terms of g. [/code]

Thoughts: OK, So we have two sets, that of the number of boy, (1,2,3...), and that of the number of girls (5,6,7,...) But how are these two sets related? I mean sure, the boys and girls exchange dances, but how do I represent that?

[code]Q2: Mike and Joey bought identical loaves of bread and packages of bologna. Mike made sandwiches of 5 slices of bologna and had 4 slices of bread left when he ran out of meat. Joey made sandwiches with 4 slices of bologna and had 4 slices of meat when he ran out of bread. How many slices of bread were in each loaf?[/code]

Thoughts: OK, So this one I feel like I was on the verge of solving. First, if we use B (bread) & M (bologona/meat) to represent our all the slices of each, then for Mike, we have that 5/m + 2/b gives one sandwich, whereas for Joey, 4/m+2/b gives one sandwich. What trips me up is when each runs out of meat, and bread, respectively. As in, how do I represent the lack of materials with my given variables? I know I should be using some form of system of equations, but how? 

[code]Q3: Sue has $3.08 in pennies, nickels, and quarters. She has four more pennies than quarters and one more nickel than pennies. How many nickels does she have? [/code]

Thoughts: Normally, in this problems, we are told how many coins there are in total, but that information is missing, and I can't seem to find a way to solve the problem. I did try expressing all other variables in terms of n, but it led to an unviable answer. 

[code]Q4: K takes 30 minutes less time than M to travel a distance of 30 miles. K travels 1/3 mile per hour faster than M. If x is K's speed in miles per hour, then find K's time for the distance in terms of x.[/code]

Thoughts: I'm totally lost.

Hello everybody!



I recently took the 2014 nationals test as practice, and I need help on the following questions.



#9The mean of 10, 4, 1, x and 1 is equal to the median. What is the smallest possible value of x? I had no idea where to start.




#13The integers 1 through 6 are to be used, each exactly once to fill the six circles in the figure so that the sums of three integers along each side of the triangle are the same. How many different solutions are possible?

(Note that two solutions are considered the same if one can be rotated or reflected to obtain the other.) I don't have the diagram for this one. I got 2, so I don't know how there are 4.




#15A square dartboard is divided into 16 congruent regions, with a point value assigned to each region as shown. Assuming each dart thrown hits the dartboard in a region, what is the probability that the sum of the points earned from three randomly thrown darts will be greater than 15? Express your answer as a common fraction. I also do not have the diagram for this one. For this one, I couldn't figure out how to correct for overcounting.




#18Alexi rolled four standard dice and lined them up to create a 4-digit number. He removed two dice from the line and rolled them again. Alexi then returned each re-rolled die to its original position in the line, thereby creating a new 4-digit number. What is the probability that the new 4-digit number is greater than the original 4-digit number? Express your answer as a common fraction. No idea where to start.




#28If f(x) = $\frac{ax + b}{cx + d}$, abcd ≠ 0 and f (f (x)) = x for all x in the domain of f, what is the value of a + d ? I tried to write some new equations and substitute it into itself, but I got nowhere.




#30The area of the largest equilateral triangle that can be inscribed in a square of

side length 1 unit can be expressed in the form $a\sqrt{b} - c$ , where a, b and c are integers. What is the value of a + b + c? My intuition told me that the triangle has one of the vertices at a vertex of the square, but I ran out of time.




All help is appreciated!

topics.title: The Creation of Mathematician PokeMathist
topics.text:
After seeing some others doing this, I decided it would be interesting to share my story of my MATHCOUNTS journey.



5th GradeI went to 6th Grade for math class, and I was really prideful and boastful about that fact. When it was time for the School Mathcounts placement test, I was really excited and nervous. When we got the results of who was in, I was so happy I made it. I didn't do anything at all, but If I knew my fellow math geniuses today, I would have worked much harder then.




6th GradeSchoolI was ready to start Mathcounts! I didn't do spectacular, because in our school the competition is always for 2nd place. 1st place was QuestForKnowledge, and still will probably be in almost everything. All the competition was for 2nd place. During our school CDR, I wasn't worried because I was expecting me to fail. To my surprise, I beat everyone who I thought was extremely better than me except QuestForKnowledge, and ended up 2nd. I took a lot of joy in the fact of how well I did. After some talks with the coach, he said that I would probably be in the team, which we found out right after CDR. Unfortunately, I didn't make the school team. I didn't do anything at all in preparation for Chapter, which I regret today. But the day had come.


ChapterChapter was really nerve racking for me, even though I kept on telling myself not to be worried, because I wouldn't make it. I wanted to make myself feel bad before the actual hard feeling so I could be prepared. Then, the results came. Somehow, I got 8th in written. I fought my position for 8th, beat the competitor to get 7th, beat the next to get 6th, but then I was up against someone different, and really good at math. The previous competitors didn't really answer at all. It was down to the tiebreaker for 5th place. There I was, staring at the answer in front of me, nervous to hit the buzzer. When my opponent hit it, my body shook and I immediately regretted not hitting it. What happened? That answer was right. My spirit was crushed at that time. I watched QuestForKnowledge win in a landslide, and I still felt really bad. I really wanted revenge. None of the team other than QFK made it into top 10, which made me consider if I actually should have been in the team. But my 6th Grade era had finished, and I was stuck with a feeling of revenge. I told myself, "I am really good at CDR. If i want to do better, I have to get better in written."



7th GradeSchoolI was ready, taking some AoPS classes but still taking it very lightly and not really studying. I was really confident at this point, maybe too confident? I got 2nd in the School MATHCOUNTS level, and I seemed happy, because i had accomplished my goal of improving my written skills.  For the school CDR, i realized I had blown it. While trying to improve my written skills, my CDR skills went down the drain. I lost in my first game(got a bye first round too cause i got 2nd in written) to someone who I know well, but in math in general, I thought that I was much better than him since he had to struggle to make it to top 12 in school, while I didn't. I was severly depressed.

You can't even imagine. I couldn't do anything at all for a long time after, my mind was blown. It was time for revenge in Chapter. Oh yeah, I also made the team.


ChapterI thought Chapter was a lot easier(mbe i improved?), and got 2nd in written. (Darn 1st was QFK again). Once it was my turn to go against 3rd, who was also in our school team, I felt fairly confident, but not too much since he had improved an immense amount in that year. Incredibly. The same problem. My CDR skills were gone. I was still speechless. I accomplished my initial goal, but in the end it backfired because my CDR skills went away. I was really sad. It seemed as if whoever I would beat in written, would easily beat me in CDR, while the opposite in 6th Grade.


StateNothin much, it was really hard. Incredibly. Although I know my ranking and my teammates rankings idk if i should share it. Im not even gonna say who did better.



Time to get back up in my CDR skills for 8th Grade, so i can finally get my revenge for these two years and the irony. I. Will. Get. REVENGE.



Also, any recommendations to improve my CDR work? Mathcounts trainer is idk meh ish working, same with Alcumus.

topics.title: Is this a well-known identity?
topics.text:
I just figured out this identity on my own, and was wondering if it has a name or something. I know that I am NOT the first person to figure this out.



The identity is as follows: $n^k -1 =(n-1)(n)^{k-1} + (n-1)(n)^{k-2} \text{ }\dots \text{ } + (n-1)(n)^0$



It is basically like saying $1000_7 - 1_{10} = 666_7$



Does this have a name? I think it is used in Number Theory.

Thanks!

topics.title: Number Sense Games for Elementary/Middle Schoolers
topics.text:
Hello AoPS Community,



I am looking for ideas on what to teach a group of elementary/middle schoolers (4th - 6th grade). I am supposed to teach number sense/basic number theory, and I would like to give my students a fun/cool number game to play with. These students are not competition math students, so the game can't be too complicated. Any ideas?



Also some more bullet point(s) when I can think of them:

* I want to teach the students about the underlying strategy of the game, and why it works (i.e. its not like a card game which is up to chance/probability). This includes simple games like NIM.

* I already have NIM as an idea. Trying to steer away from games like 24 (where you basically have to do guesswork).
